scope_note: No web access (AR-003). This matrix covers only the prior-benchmark comparison the source paper itself makes (project/paper.txt Section 3); it is not an independent systematic search, and the Gap statement in story/lit_gap_chain.md is scoped accordingly.

dimension_matrix.problem_framing: Simple, portable MCU-class performance benchmarking using real algorithms (not ML-specific)
dimension_matrix.method_family: Fixed C-code kernels (e.g., list processing, matrix manipulation, CRC)
dimension_matrix.key_assumption: A short, generic workload is representative enough of MCU performance
dimension_matrix.data_eval: No dataset; a fixed synthetic workload
dimension_matrix.strength: Easy to implement and port; widely adopted as the MCU performance standard
dimension_matrix.weakness_limit: Does not profile full programs and does not represent ML inference workloads
dimension_matrix.relation_to_mlperf_tiny: Establishes that an MCU-class benchmark tradition exists, but not one that measures ML inference

dimension_matrix.problem_framing: Benchmarking real ML inference workloads on edge-class devices
dimension_matrix.method_family: Standard ML inference models run end-to-end
dimension_matrix.key_assumption: Edge-class devices have on the order of gigabytes of memory available
dimension_matrix.data_eval: Real ML models/datasets, but at edge- (not MCU-) scale
dimension_matrix.strength: Uses actual ML inference workloads, unlike CoreMark; also has a companion power benchmark (ULPMark-CM) for CoreMark
dimension_matrix.weakness_limit: Models require far too much memory (GBs) and have long runtimes for MCU-class devices; MLMark itself has no power measurement
dimension_matrix.relation_to_mlperf_tiny: Closest in spirit (real ML workloads) but not deployable on, or representative of, MCU-class hardware

dimension_matrix.problem_framing: Community-driven, cross-industry ML inference benchmarking at scale
dimension_matrix.method_family: Standard large-model inference benchmarks across datacenter/mobile-class systems
dimension_matrix.key_assumption: Systems under test have the memory and compute of mobile/server-class hardware
dimension_matrix.data_eval: Standard large-scale ML benchmarks; only planning to add power measurement
dimension_matrix.strength: Broad, well-governed, industry-wide inference benchmarking effort
dimension_matrix.weakness_limit: Precludes MCUs and other resource-constrained platforms for lack of small benchmarks and compatible implementations
dimension_matrix.relation_to_mlperf_tiny: The parent MLPerf effort; MLPerf Tiny extends it downward to microcontroller-class hardware

organizing_dimensions_chosen: whether the workload represents real ML inference (vs. generic code)
whether the memory/compute envelope matches MCU-class devices
whether power/energy is measured as a first-class metric
why_these_dimensions: These three dimensions are exactly the axes on which the source paper itself distinguishes MLPerf Tiny from each prior benchmark (project/paper.txt, Section 3); no additional dimensions were introduced, consistent with the no-web literature-scope constraint (AR-003).
